title: Negatives and Questions Quiz 4
description: Use will, going to, will be and will have in negatives and questions, and keep the present tense after if and until.
instructions: Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which question is correct?
questions.explanation: Will + subject + base verb. Watch out: will is never followed by to, and it needs no do.

questions.question: Make the negative: 'She is going to buy a car.'
options: She isn't going to buy a car.
She doesn't going to buy a car.
She won't going to buy a car.
She isn't go to buy a car.
questions.explanation: Negative of be going to: is not + going to + base verb. Watch out: the helper is is, not does or won't.

questions.question: {{1}} she {{2}} (work) at eight tomorrow? Use the future continuous.
questions.explanation: The future continuous question is Will + subject + be + verb-ing. Watch out: only will moves, and be stays behind the subject.

questions.question: I {{1}} (not / tell) anyone. I promise.
questions.explanation: A promise uses will, so the negative is will not + base verb. Watch out: won't is followed by tell, not told or telling.

questions.question: 'If it won't rain, we will go to the park' is correct.
questions.explanation: After if, the present simple is used, so the sentence is If it doesn't rain, we will go to the park. Watch out: will is never used in the if clause.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I won't call you until she will arrive.
I won't to call you until she arrives.
I won't call you until she doesn't arrive.
I won't call you until she arrives.
questions.explanation: After until, the present simple expresses the future: until she arrives. Watch out: neither will nor a second negative is used after until.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative helper.

rows.given: I ___ going to wait any longer.
She ___ going to pass the exam.
I ___ forget your birthday. I promise.

questions.explanation: Going to takes am, is or are. A promise or a prediction with no going to takes will. Watch out: He ___ be needs will not, because is not be is never used.

questions.question: Match each future form with its question formula.
right: Am / Is / Are + subject + going to + base verb
questions.explanation: Only the first helper moves in front of the subject. Watch out: the future perfect question uses will + subject + have, not has.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order to make a question.
questions.explanation: Will goes first, then the subject, then have + past participle. Watch out: by Friday is the time phrase and stays at the end.

questions.question: Look at those black clouds! Which question fits?
questions.explanation: We can see the rain coming, so be going to is used: Is it going to rain? Watch out: going to takes the base verb, with no extra to or do.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: Will she be waiting for us?
Will they finish have by six?
questions.explanation: The correct ones keep the helper before the subject and use the right verb form. Watch out: will is followed by the base verb, so arrived is wrong.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: Will she goes to the party?
accepted: Will she go to the party?
Will she go to the party
questions.explanation: After will the verb is in the base form: Will she go? Watch out: will never takes -s.
